quote.text: Let death and exile and every other thing which appears dreadful be daily before your eyes; but most of all death: and you will never think of anything mean nor will you desire anything extravagantly.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Embrace the daily reminder of life's transience to cherish every moment with your children and cultivate gratitude.
    • Allow the awareness of mortality to guide you in teaching young minds about the value of modesty, responsibility, and resilience.
  • Leadership:
    • Let the contemplation of impermanence keep your decisions grounded and help you focus on what truly matters rather than getting distracted by fleeting ambitions.
    • Recognize that a leader's humility and focus on core virtues guard against the pitfalls of vanity and impractical extravagance.
  • Product Management:
    • In managing products, reflect on the impermanence of trends to prioritize sustainable, high-value improvements over short-lived fads.
    • Use the perspective of life's brevity to drive innovative yet pragmatic choices, ensuring that every feature or update genuinely serves the user.
